heading.en: Where does he find the time?

hook.en: A professor who writes scholarly books, essays and best-selling novels is asked how he manages it all. His answer is a single word: interstices.

objectives.en: Introduce Umberto Eco and his work
Explain what Eco means by interstices

narration.en: A professor who writes scholarly books, essays and best-selling novels is asked how he manages it all. His answer is a single word: interstices.

body.en: Umberto Eco was an Italian scholar and novelist and a professor at the University of Bologna. He was famous for his academic work on semiotics, the study of signs, as well as on literary interpretation and medieval aesthetics. He also wrote novels, the most famous being The Name of the Rose, which sold millions of copies around the world.

points.en: Professor at the University of Bologna
Fields: semiotics, literary interpretation, medieval aesthetics
Best-known novel: The Name of the Rose

narration.en: Umberto Eco was an Italian scholar and novelist and a professor at the University of Bologna. He was famous for his academic work on semiotics, the study of signs, as well as on literary interpretation and medieval aesthetics. Let us picture how small gaps in a day add up for Eco.

say.en: Waiting for the lift in the morning: a few minutes to think and write.
A few spare minutes before a lecture.

text.en: Before a lecture: a few minutes

say.en: Waiting for a visitor to arrive: another gap.
Put together, these gaps add up to real working time.

text.en: Gaps add up to real work

say.en: And on Sundays, he says, he writes novels.

body.en: When the interviewer asks how he does so much, Eco says he uses the interstices: the empty spaces in a day. Our lives are full of small gaps, such as the minutes spent waiting for a lift or for someone to arrive, and he uses them to work. He also says he sees himself mainly as a university professor who writes novels on Sundays.

points.en: Interstices: small empty spaces in time
Example: waiting for a lift or a visitor
Sees himself as a professor who writes novels on Sundays

problem.en: What are interstices, and how does Eco use them?

steps.en: Define: small empty spaces or gaps in time.
Give an example: waiting for a lift or for a guest.
Say how he uses them: he writes and works during these gaps.

answer.en: Interstices are the small empty spaces in our day, such as the time spent waiting for a lift or a visitor. Eco uses these gaps to work, which is how he manages to do so much.
